rationale: Start with a broad mid-strength scouting gradient and moderate temperature to spread unknown compounds across the run while still eluting strongly retained species by 42 min. This gives an informative first map of elution coverage, peak spacing, and whether the sample needs weaker/stronger starting conditions or a shallower gradient next.

All 10 compounds eluted with baseline resolution and the run finished very early, so the limiting factor is analysis time; a weaker, much shallower gradient should retain compounds longer and compress the empty late window less aggressively, potentially improving the time term while preserving full elution. Keeping phi0 and T fixed isolates the effect of gradient strength/slope on the clustered mid-run region around peaks 5–7.

Injection 1 already had perfect resolution, so we should optimize only the time term by making the gradient steeper and slightly less strong at the end to trim total analysis time without risking loss of late peaks. This targets a modest left-shift from the 12.7 min last peak while preserving the excellent spacing in the 5–8 min cluster.

The current best run is very fast but slightly under-resolves peaks 6 and 7, so a small increase in gradient time should selectively improve resolution in the crowded middle without reintroducing a time penalty. Holding phi0, phi1, and T constant makes this a focused local optimization around the strong candidate method.

We have already reached the maximum CRF, so the only sensible remaining move is to test robustness around the optimum; a small temperature decrease may slightly increase selectivity in the tight 6/7 region while likely keeping the method in the zero time-penalty regime. This checks whether the optimum is broad or whether 40 C is uniquely favorable.

Lowering temperature worsened selectivity dramatically, so the informative robustness counterpart is a small increase to 45 C to see whether the optimum is centered near 40 C or improves on the high-temperature side. Keeping the already optimal gradient fixed isolates temperature effects on the critical middle cluster.

With temperature clearly worse on either side of 40 C, test a slightly weaker final organic composition while keeping the optimal timing and temperature fixed; this should modestly expand the crowded middle-to-late region and may preserve a zero time penalty. It is a local selectivity check around an already perfect method rather than a broad exploration.

The optimum appears sensitive mainly in the crowded early-middle section, so increasing phi0 slightly while keeping the successful slope and endpoint fixed may decompress that cluster and test whether the perfect score is robust to a stronger start. This is a targeted local perturbation of initial elution strength around the current best method.

A modest increase in phi0 from 0.10 to 0.15 preserved a perfect score and shortened the run, so one more step higher probes whether the zero-penalty optimum extends to a stronger starting condition or begins to compress the critical 6/7 pair. This is a focused boundary test around the current robust optimum family.

Since raising phi0 further began to erode the critical resolution, keep the successful 0.15 start and test a slightly stronger phi1 to see whether run time can be trimmed without dropping the minimum pair below baseline separation. This maps the upper-end robustness of the now clearly optimal neighborhood.

The best region is clearly centered near phi0 0.15, phi1 0.85, 40 C, so a slightly longer gradient checks whether we can gain extra robustness on the critical 6/7 pair while staying in the zero time-penalty zone. This helps define how broad the plateau of perfect methods is around the optimum.

A longer gradient incurred a time penalty, so the remaining useful local check is the shorter side of the optimum to define the lower tG boundary around the perfect method. This tests whether the 0.15 start can maintain full resolution at a faster program than the current best.

The optimum has been bracketed in tG and phi1 on the stronger side, so testing a slightly weaker phi1 at the best phi0 and tG maps the other side of the local optimum. This should indicate whether 0.85 is truly centered or whether selectivity for the critical 6/7 pair improves without introducing a time penalty.

A slightly weaker endpoint than 0.80 tests the last unexplored nearby boundary around the perfect method while keeping the proven phi0, tG, and T fixed. This should show whether selectivity in the critical 6/7 region can improve further without pushing t_last far enough to incur a meaningful time penalty.

We have mapped the optimum on the stronger-start side, so the complementary local boundary test is a weaker start at the same successful endpoint, time, and temperature. This will show whether 0.15 is truly near the center of a broad plateau or whether additional early retention can preserve full resolution without harming the time term.

The optimum at 40 C is established, but we have not yet checked whether a larger temperature shift changes selectivity qualitatively rather than incrementally. A low-temperature probe can reveal whether the critical pair behavior is monotonic or whether an alternate selectivity regime exists, while all compounds are very likely still within the run window.

Since 25 C revealed a very different and much worse selectivity regime, the matching high-temperature extreme is the most informative remaining global probe. This determines whether 40 C is a local optimum between two bad regimes or whether selectivity recovers at the hot end.

With temperature extremes clearly inferior and the optimum family already established, a final useful local test is whether a slightly longer gradient rescues the 0.10-start method into the perfect region. This checks if phi0 0.10 can match the best robustness when compensated by a modestly shallower slope.

A weaker start with phi1 0.85 came close to perfect, so pairing that low phi0 with a slightly stronger endpoint tests whether the time penalty can be removed while preserving baseline resolution. This explores the only nearby combination not yet mapped in the high-performing region.

The strongest nearby endpoints tested so far still keep all compounds in range, so probing phi1 0.95 at a proven start condition maps the upper gradient-strength limit of the high-CRF region. This checks whether the perfect method plateau extends to a more aggressive endpoint or whether the critical pair compresses too far.

The only remaining nearby high-performance corner not yet tested is the combination of the best start composition with the strongest endpoint. This will complete the local map around the optimum and confirm whether phi0 0.15 remains favorable when the gradient is made maximally strong.

To complete the local response surface around the best family, test the low-phi0 and low-phi1 corner that remains unmeasured. This assesses whether the extra early retention from phi0 0.05 can be offset by a weaker endpoint to improve the critical pair or whether time penalty dominates.

Most nearby combinations around the optimum have been mapped except the stronger-start, weaker-end corner. Testing phi0 0.20 with phi1 0.80 will complete that local grid and show whether the resolution loss seen at higher phi0 is driven mainly by the start strength or by the stronger endpoint.

Now that phi0 0.20 with phi1 0.80 also gives a perfect score, testing phi1 0.75 defines how far the zero-penalty plateau extends toward a weaker endpoint at this stronger start. This refines the boundary of the optimal region and checks whether robustness improves or time penalty appears.

With only one injection left and several perfect methods already found, the most useful final test is to probe whether the perfect plateau extends one more step to a stronger start at the successful phi1 0.80. This cleanly defines the upper phi0 boundary of the best-performing region while staying close to the proven optimum family.
